evals.name: new-evm-minimal-executable
evals.prompt: Create a complete Effectstream template named `my-evm-rooms` at `/tmp/eval-runs/my-evm-rooms/`. Use EVM with local Hardhat only, no batcher, no frontend, and no mainnet config. Add `createRoom(roomName: string up to 32 chars, maxPlayers: number 2-8)`, persist rooms, expose a GET API, include mandatory Phase A/B tests, and add Docker because I explicitly want it. Resolve the latest stable coordinated @effectstream version from npm. Do not stop at writing files: run bun install, build contracts, generate pgtyped files, boot bun run dev to a known indexing state, and run the tests. Use only generated typed queries, including tests and readiness checks. Report the exact verification trail.
evals.expected_output: An executable project, not a partial skeleton. The root manifest pins the exact version returned by npm uniformly, declares workspace dependencies, and provides effectstream.default/build scripts. start.dev.ts uses { cwd }. packages/database owns migrations and every SQL query; generated queries are produced by build:pgtypes and tests import them through @my-evm-rooms/database without db.query or inline SQL. Phase B submits a real Effectstream L2 contract transaction and proves the typed DB result plus GET API. Docker is present because requested. The report includes actual command outcomes for install, build:evm, build:pgtypes, dev boot/indexing, test, and Docker verification rather than suggested commands.

evals.name: new-multichain-evm-midnight-executable
evals.prompt: Create and verify a complete Effectstream template named `mint-and-mint` at `/tmp/eval-runs/mint-and-mint/`. Target EVM (Hardhat dev, Arbitrum mainnet) and Midnight. Users mint an ERC-721 on EVM and increment a Midnight counter. Include an EVM Effectstream L2 batcher, Vite/React frontend, typed `NftMinted` app events, Phase A/B/C tests, mainnet configs, and Docker. Use the purpose-named package `packages/app-events`, not a generic shared package. Use security namespace `mint-and-mint` consistently in frontend EffectstreamConfig, BatcherConfig, and node ConfigBuilder. Resolve the latest stable @effectstream version from npm and run the full install/build/pgtyped/dev/test/Docker verification trail. Phase B must submit through /send-input and use generated typed queries to prove the row appears.
evals.expected_output: A complete runnable EVM+Midnight project. packages/app-events is named @mint-and-mint/app-events and is consumed through workspace:* by node/frontend; no packages/shared exists. The three L2 namespace sites all use mint-and-mint. The L2 primitive omits stateMachinePrefix. start.dev.ts uses { cwd }, includes an explicit Midnight compile phase only if the npm-resolved launchMidnight still requires it, and orders dependent services correctly. SQL exists only under the database package, pgtyped output is generated, and Phase B exercises batcher admission, chain submission, L2 node re-verification, STM, typed DB read, and API. Phase C opens the built UI. Mainnet files validate env vars and contain the production placeholder warning. The final report contains actual successful or exact failed command evidence.

evals.name: migrate-paimaexample-chess
evals.prompt: I have an old `@paimaexample/*` chess template at `/tmp/eval-runs/legacy-chess/` with the standard nested client/shared layout. Produce a concrete migration plan at `/tmp/eval-runs/legacy-chess-migration-plan.md`. Explain how to flatten the app, replace Paima APIs, remove round/match/tick executor layers, move database effects into the STM, and decide whether pure chess rules stay beside the node or become a purpose-named `packages/chess-rules` package when both node and frontend consume them. Do not create a generic shared/utils/common package. Require all application, recovery, readiness, and test queries to be pgtyped. The completed migration must resolve the latest stable @effectstream version from npm and pass install, contract build, pgtyped generation, dev boot, Phase A/B/C tests, and Docker verification.
evals.expected_output: An ordered file-level migration plan covering @paimaexample to @effectstream API changes, flat packages/node and packages/database ownership, removal of packages/client and generic packages/shared wrappers, removal of executor abstractions, direct World.resolve calls, and a justified ownership decision for reusable chess rules. It forbids inline SQL in TypeScript and specifies typed test queries. It adds root start.dev.ts, environment-specific node entry/config files, mandatory tests, and Docker. It resolves @effectstream from npm rather than copying a template version and defines executable acceptance criteria for every verification command.

evals.name: new-cardano-mint-burn-executable
evals.prompt: Create and verify a Cardano-only Effectstream template named `cardano-native-assets` at `/tmp/eval-runs/cardano-native-assets/`. Use YACI+Dolos with CARDANO_UTXORPC_PARALLEL and CardanoMintBurn; no EVM, no batcher, and no custom on-chain contract. The frontend should create/fund a local wallet and submit a native asset mint directly. Persist transaction id, metadata, assets, input addresses, and output addresses, expose a GET API, and include Phase A/B/C tests. Phase B must submit a real mint and read the result with generated typed queries. Resolve @effectstream versions from npm and run install, pgtyped generation, dev boot, and tests.
evals.expected_output: A runnable Cardano template whose grammar and STM use the current CardanoMintBurn payload fields txId, metadata, assets, inputAddresses, and outputAddresses rather than policy/asset/quantity. launchCardano uses { cwd }, the dev config deliberately handles CARDANO_SUBMIT_TX, and the frontend uses the YACI adaAmount faucet field. All SQL and test/readiness queries are authored under packages/database and generated by pgtyped. The verification report proves YACI/Dolos readiness, a real mint-to-STM-to-typed-DB-to-API round trip, and a browser interaction.

evals.name: new-solana-sponsored-program-phases
evals.prompt: Create and verify a Solana template named `solana-sponsored-counter` at `/tmp/eval-runs/solana-sponsored-counter/`. Include a compiled counter program, SOLANA_RPC_PARALLEL, SolanaProgramLog, a SolanaAdapter sponsor batcher, and a Vite/React frontend. Add explicit one-shot orchestrator programs for building the SBF program, creating or reusing the sponsor wallet, and funding it before the batcher starts. Put substantial wallet provisioning code in a purpose-named `packages/wallet-provisioning` package; do not create shared/common/utils. Make setup idempotent. Include Phase A/B/C tests and only generated typed database queries. Resolve @effectstream from npm and execute install, program build, pgtyped, dev boot, and tests.
evals.expected_output: A runnable Solana project using ConfigNetworkType.SOLANA, SOLANA_RPC_PARALLEL, launchSolana from @effectstream/orchestrator/scripts/launch-solana, and SolanaNames gates. start.dev.ts has an explicit dependency graph build-program/validator -> create-sponsor-wallet -> fund-sponsor-wallet -> batcher -> frontend; setup phases use waitToExit true and are idempotent. Phase A verifies the program artifact, wallet, and balance. Phase B uses the real sponsored batcher path and a typed DB assertion. No generic shared package or inline TypeScript SQL exists, and the final report contains actual command evidence.

evals.name: new-celestia-batcher-executable
evals.prompt: Create and verify an indexer-focused Effectstream template named `celestia-blobs` at `/tmp/eval-runs/celestia-blobs/`. Use CELESTIA_PARALLEL, PrimitiveTypeCelestiaGeneric, and CelestiaAdapter, with no frontend and no Docker. Include the Celestia bridge/funding launcher phases, a GET API, and mandatory Phase A/B tests. Phase B must submit through the batcher and wait for a generated typed query to observe the blob. Resolve @effectstream from npm and run install, pgtyped, dev boot, and tests with realistic Celestia cold-start/long-poll timeouts.
evals.expected_output: A runnable purpose-scoped indexer template with launchCelestia/CelestiaNames, CelestiaAdapter, explicit bridge funding dependency, no unnecessary frontend/contracts from unrelated chains, and no generic shared package. SQL is restricted to database .sql/migrations and every TypeScript caller uses generated prepared queries. Phase B covers /send-input through PFB submission, primitive, STM, typed DB read, and API. Verification uses long enough startup and assertion budgets and reports actual outcomes.
